blocks.text:
After breakfast, explore Quito and head towards Rucu Pichincha. The complete day, including transfers, takes approximately eight hours; the city sightseeing portion lasts about four hours.

Quito stands at roughly 2,850 metres above sea level. Founded in the 16th century on the remains of an Inca city, its colonial historic centre is one of Latin America's best preserved and among the earliest UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Walk past churches, squares, domes and historic buildings as your guide explains the architecture, culture and Quito School of Art, shaped by Spanish, Italian, Moorish, Flemish and local traditions.

On Plaza Grande, see the Cathedral, Presidential Palace, Archbishop's Palace and City Hall. Visit the San Francisco church and a Jesuit church with an intricately carved façade. The Franciscan complex is closely linked to Quito's colonial history and its school of painting and sculpture, whose artists combined European techniques with local motifs. Continue to El Panecillo for views over the old and new districts, valleys and surrounding hills, near the winged statue of the Virgin Mary.

Later take the TelefériQo, a cable car that rises from around 2,950 to 4,100 metres over approximately 2.5 km, to Cruz Loma on the slopes of Pichincha. Enjoy a short walk across the páramo and, in clear weather, views of Cotopaxi, Antisana, Cayambe and other volcanoes.

A boxed lunch is included. Accommodation in Quito is at Hotel Patio Andaluz or Mercure, subject to confirmation. Meals: breakfast and boxed lunch.
